However, the supplied evidence is mostly cross-system and does not provide a head-to-head TEA versus TEOA comparison within one unchanged Co(II)-bipyridine CO2-photoreduction formulation. Methods exist to observe donor-derived radicals and charge-carrier responses, but their transfer to the target cobalt system remains unvalidated, so discrimination is plausible but not yet directly established."},{"question_id":"Q2","mechanism_evidence_ids":["EV059","EV027","EV048","EV051","EV085","GX016","GX001","GX005","GX011"],"method_evidence_ids":["EV004","EV052","EV076","EV088","GX008"],"status":"partial","reason":"The dataset supports catalyst-speciation and interaction hypotheses in cobalt photocatalysis, including possible donor coordination, altered local environment, deactivation, or active-species ambiguity. It also contains transferable operando and solution-characterization methods with actual observables for coordination environment and catalyst state. But there is no direct evidence that TEA versus TEOA changes Co(II)-bipyridine identity or stability under matched target conditions, so the family is only partially supported."},{"question_id":"Q3","mechanism_evidence_ids":["EV007","EV011","EV053","EV065","EV041","EV095","EV071","GX007","GX018"],"method_evidence_ids":["EV053","EV018","EV005","EV077"],"status":"partial","reason":"This family has strong transferable mechanistic support that sacrificial donors influence reductive quenching, reduced-intermediate formation, lifetimes, and electron-transfer routes, with explicit donor-side chemistry for TEOA and both TEA/TEOA radical formation. It also has usable methods: fluorescence or UV-vis quenching, transient absorption, and luminescence quenching all provide concrete observables and route discrimination. Yet the evidence is not a direct TEA-versus-TEOA demonstration in the target Co(II)-bipyridine CO2-reduction system, so support remains partial rather than complete."},{"question_id":"Q4","mechanism_evidence_ids":["EV021","EV029","EV031","EV063","EV024","GX011"],"method_evidence_ids":["EV080","EV004","EV068","GX008"],"status":"partial","reason":"The evidence supports considering additive-dependent effects on CO2 interaction, intermediate stability, and assignment ambiguity, including isotope-bounded origin checks and cross-system proposals that TEOA can assist CO2 trapping or alter intermediate populations. Transferable operando FTIR/Raman/XAS strategies with isotope substitution offer real discriminating observables for assignment. However, the supplied literature does not directly identify substrate-bound intermediates in a Co(II)-bipyridine TEA/TEOA comparison, so the question family is only partially covered."},{"question_id":"Q5","mechanism_evidence_ids":["EV059","EV021","EV046","EV081","EV045","EV063","EV022","EV069","GX012"],"method_evidence_ids":["EV046","EV081","EV082","GX008"],"status":"supported","reason":"This family is the best supported. The supplied evidence directly addresses photocatalytic CO/H2 outputs, no-component controls, catalyst-free background contributions, CO2 versus Ar or dark controls, and 13CO2 origin verification across related CO2-reduction systems. The methods are usable and discriminating: GC for CO/H2 quantification, GC-MS with 13CO2 for origin, and explicit omission controls to separate component contributions. Although the exact TEA-versus-TEOA difference in a single matched Co(II)-bipyridine system still needs confirmation, both the question family and a plausible characterization/discrimination method are present."},{"question_id":"Q6","mechanism_evidence_ids":["EV061","EV029","EV041","EV013","EV024","GX010","GX015","GX019","GX009"],"method_evidence_ids":["EV080","GX010","EV053"],"status":"partial","reason":"The literature supports multiple non-electron-donation roles for TEOA or related amines: proton relay or proton-source effects, CO2 capture/adduct chemistry, coordination effects, and medium-property changes. But no supplied study cleanly decouples electron donation from these other roles for TEA versus TEOA in a matched Co(II)-bipyridine photocatalytic CO2-reduction system, so the family remains partial."}],"supplement_queries":[]}
